retention: Matched control for ADD-immediate lowering and gadget layout changes, sharing its body with the ideal gadget ceiling bench.
Private-counter control for direct atomic lowering and multicore scaling.
Matched control for guest_call_deep_chain_loop.S: the same 128 functions, calls and returns as eight chains of sixteen.
Calls a chain of 128 framed functions, each calling the next from its own site, deeper than a host return-address stack holds. Every return runs an epilogue head.
Matched control for guest_call_leaf_walk_loop.S: the same call sites called in index order, so every call and return is predictable.

Calls eight framed leaves from sixty-four sites in a pseudo-random order, so both the callee and the return's successor are unpredictable and every return runs an epilogue head, as compiled code calling small functions does.
Matched control for guest_call_site_loop.S: the same loop and leaf with the call and the return replaced by direct branches.
Calls one leaf from one site in a loop, so the host predicts the callee and the return's successor. A change to calls and returns must not slow it.
Guest CMP-immediate followed by B.cond, the shape a translated block ends on. The loop counters in the other probes are subs with a real destination and so never take the fused path.

Guest CMP of two registers followed by B.cond. G116 ranks this pair fourth and ninth over a full Geekbench run while the immediate form does not reach the table, so the two shapes get separate probes.
Private compare-and-retry control for exclusive sequence quality.
Exercises the shared load-result and store-status register fallback shape.

Eight words from eight gadget families, each with one successor: the predictable control for guest_dispatch_arity_2_loop.S and guest_dispatch_arity_3_loop.S, which run the same words the same number of times.
The arity probe words in an order that gives about half of them two successors.

The arity probe words in an order that gives nearly every one three successors, so the dispatch that ends each gadget mispredicts inside one block at a rate the order sets. The link and indirect probes mispredict only at block ends.
Matched control for guest_epilogue_frame_loop.S: the same instructions, with one body instruction between the epilogue's ADD SP and its RET, so the restores are not a run that ends in the return.

Calls a leaf whose 96-byte frame is popped by six LDP at offsets and ADD SP right before its RET, the most frequent epilogue in Geekbench and Clang. Measures the restores and return of a call-heavy frame as one run.
Matched control for guest_epilogue_hint_loop.S: the same instructions, with one body instruction between the epilogue's restores and its AUTIASP.
guest_epilogue_pair_loop.S's leaf built for pointer authentication: PACIASP on entry and AUTIASP between the restores and the RET, hints the virtual CPU runs as NOPs.
Matched control for guest_epilogue_pair_loop.S: the same instructions, with one body instruction between the epilogue's restores and its RET.
Calls a leaf whose two-pair frame is popped by LDP at an offset and LDP X29, X30 post-index right before its RET, the short epilogue of common leaves.
Measures floating-state activation and restoration overhead.
Measures a run of native floating-point operations sharing one program-level environment activation.
Measures vector-state successor linking through a conditional self-edge.
Stresses floating-state exits at a polymorphic indirect branch site.
Matched DC-CVAU execution-boundary control for exact gadget-cache validation without advancing the guest code-change sequence.
Uses IC IVAU on unchanged code every iteration to measure exact reuse of stale gadget programs after the guest code-change sequence advances.
Matched DC-CVAU control for the link-population probe: same chain walk and same execution boundary without advancing the guest code-change sequence.

Walks a chain of thousands of distinct single-branch blocks once so the link table carries a standing population, then runs the IC IVAU loop. The other invalidation probe names only a handful of targets, so it cannot measure how the link reset scales with translated code.
Cycles one ADD-immediate gadget's indirect dispatch through eight distinct successor gadget families to isolate G107's early-target-fetch hypothesis.
Matched DC-CVAU control for the reindex probe: same full-size block and execution boundary without advancing the guest code-change sequence, so no reactivation occurs.

Reactivates a full-size translated block every iteration so the stream index walk, which scales with program size rather than with guest work, is measurable. The other invalidation probes time a four-instruction block that spans one or two index granules.
Matched control for guest_gpr_memory_mixed_loop: the same loads, stores and ALU work at the same offsets, each transfer through a base register of its own.
Same-base scalar loads and stores through x13, each followed by an ALU instruction, so every transfer after the first of a loop follows one through the same unwritten base.
Matched control for guest_gpr_memory_run_loop: the same loads and stores at the same offsets, each through a base register of its own, so no transfer follows another through the same base.
Measures same-page scalar memory runs through an allocated base register.
Measures monomorphic indirect-call and return successor linking.
Matched control for in-place ADD-immediate lowering, interleaving three chains so no adjacent forward is selected and every word reaches its guest register through CpuState.

Matched control for unsigned-offset transfers whose transferred register is a baked CpuState displacement. Three load/modify/store chains run interleaved through one same-page buffer, so no adjacent forward is ever selected and every value crosses CpuState between the load that produced it and the store that consumes it.
Matched control for same-page native integer pair transfers.
Matched control for guest_integer_pair_memory_run_loop: the same LDP, LDPSW and STP at the same offsets, each through a base register of its own.
Same-base GPR pairs: four LDP and LDPSW through one base, then four STP through another, so every pair after the first of a loop follows one through the same unwritten base.

ISB then MRS CNTVCT_EL0, the counter read of arm64 Linux's vDSO without FEAT_ECV. The only probe that runs an ISB, so the only one that measures the code-change sequence check both engines make at a context synchronization point.
Baseline for cached direct successor-link throughput.

Matched control for guest_link_walk_loop.S: the same blocks and instructions walked in index order, so the linked branches' successors are predictable and the difference between the two is their misprediction.

Walks sixty-four small blocks in a pseudo-random order, two direct branches a step, each linking to a successor that begins with one of eight families, so both mispredict at a rate the order sets. The other link probes are loops whose successor the host predicts, so they cannot measure what a link follow costs when it mispredicts.
Matched control for logical-register move alias lowering.

Maps an anonymous region, faults in and checks every page, and unmaps it, as allocators and loaders return memory. Measures publishing and removing host mappings and the software TLB range invalidation an unmap causes.
Measures repeated scalar and vector accesses at stable translated sites.

Walks four times the software TLB's capacity from threads sharing one address space, so every access is a miss and the software-MMU translate path is measured under the concurrency the multi-core phase produces.
Matched control for guest_move_chain_loop.S: the same instructions, with another instruction between every two moves.
Rows of three 64-bit register moves that each read the previous one's destination, so the ordinary words forward a register into, through and out of every move.
MOVK at every halfword position and EXTR at both widths plus the ROR alias, in the loop body. The other integer probes reach these entries only while materialising their iteration count.
Matched control for guest_move_mixed2_loop.S: the same instructions, with another instruction between the two moves.
Rows of a 64-bit and then a 32-bit register move, the commonest row of mixed widths in Geekbench and Clang.
Matched control for guest_move_mixed3_loop.S: the same instructions, with another instruction between every two moves.
Rows of two 64-bit and then one 32-bit register move.
Matched control for guest_move_row2_loop.S: the same instructions, with another instruction between the two moves.
Rows of two 64-bit register moves between the instruction that feeds the first and the one that reads the last, the commonest row in Geekbench and Clang.
Matched control for guest_move_row3_loop.S: the same instructions, with another instruction between every two moves.
Rows of three 64-bit register moves between the instruction that feeds the first and the one that reads the last.
Matched control for guest_move_row4_loop.S: the same instructions, with another instruction between every two moves.
Rows of four 64-bit register moves between the instruction that feeds the first and the one that reads the last.
Matched control for guest_move_row6_loop.S: the same instructions, with another instruction between every two moves.
Rows of six 64-bit register moves between the instruction that feeds the first and the one that reads the last.
Matched control for guest_narrow_memory_run_loop: the same byte, halfword and sign-extending transfers at the same offsets, each through a base register of its own.
Same-base byte, halfword and sign-extending unsigned-offset loads and stores through x13, so every transfer after the first of a loop follows one through the same unwritten base.
Measures translation-predecoded scalar operand addressing.

The ADRP plus ADD address idiom in a loop. G113 measured it as the third most frequent adjacent gadget pair in translated code, and the other probes use it once each on their way out rather than in a loop.
Rotates one BLR site through thirty-two targets, more than any site's cells hold, as virtual calls and handler dispatch do. Pairs with guest_indirect_link_loop.S as the monomorphic control.

Matched control for guest_prologue_frame_loop.S: the same instructions, with one body instruction between the prologue's stores and its ADD X29, so the stores are not a run that ends in the frame pointer.

Calls a leaf whose 96-byte frame is stored by SUB SP and six STP at offsets right before its ADD X29, SP, the most frequent prologue in Geekbench and Clang. Measures the saves and frame pointer of a call-heavy frame as one run.
Matched control for guest_prologue_pair_loop.S: the same instructions, with one body instruction between the prologue's stores and its MOV X29, SP.
Calls a leaf whose 32-byte frame is pushed by STP X29, X30 pre-index and STR of one register right before its MOV X29, SP, the short prologue of leaves that save one register.
Exercises the software reservation fallback followed by publication.
Exercises the bounded native reservation sequence followed by publication.
Matched control for guest_return_skip_walk_loop.S: the same call sites called in index order.
As guest_return_walk_loop.S, but every return lands one instruction past its call's return address, so it misses the return ring and is followed from the address space's target table.
Matched control for guest_return_walk_loop.S: the same call sites called in index order, so the return's successor is predictable.

Calls one leaf from sixty-four sites in a pseudo-random order, so its return, found on the return ring, links to one of eight successor families and mispredicts at a rate the order sets. guest_indirect_link_loop.S returns to one site, which the host predicts.

A parent and a forked child pinned to one CPU hand a byte back and forth over pipes and each touch a small working set, so every hand-off switches one vCPU's software TLB between address spaces. The only probe whose cost is the TLB flush and refill a context switch causes.
Matched control for the page-contained scalar byte fast path.

Realistic scalar mix (loads, stores, pairs, narrow accesses, flag-setting ALU, selects, a never-taken check and two data-dependent skips) sharing its body with the ideal gadget ceiling bench and printing the checksum, path counts and retired instructions the host bench must reproduce.
Measures basic vector floating arithmetic register addressing.
Matched out-of-bank control for the destination-resident integer MLA run.
Measures a 32-instruction integer MLA run with one repeated v0 destination and nonaliasing sources.
Measures indexed vector multiply-add register addressing.

Realistic FP/SIMD mix (vector pair and register-offset transfers, indexed and vector FMLA, converts, an FP compare branch) sharing its body with the ideal gadget ceiling bench and printing the checksum, path counts and retired instructions the host bench must reproduce.
Measures signed pairwise-add-long vector lowering.
Measures signed widening-multiply vector lowering.
Measures one-register structure transfers with remapped vector state.
Two-table control for one-table lookup specialization changes.
Measures one-table vector lookup operand addressing.
Measures same-width three-register vector addition lowering.
Matched control for guest_simd_unsigned_memory_run_loop: the same 128-bit loads and stores at the same offsets, each through a base register of its own.
Measures same-page unsigned-offset vector memory runs.
Measures adjacent scalar memory runs addressed directly from SP.

Repeated getpid, the cheapest syscall the guest kernel offers, so the loop measures the guest entry boundary rather than the work behind it. The only probe that exercises the per-entry thread execution state resolution.

Load-acquire through a top-byte-tagged pointer beside a plain load of the same page, as a tagged heap object read both ways, and both use the read half of the page's TLB entry. With an argument the pointer is untagged, the matched control. Needs top-byte ignore, the emulator's default.

LSE atomic through a top-byte-tagged pointer beside a plain store to the same page, and both use the write half of the page's TLB entry. With an argument the pointer is untagged, the matched control. Needs top-byte ignore, the emulator's default.

LSE atomic through a top-byte-tagged pointer alone on its page, the cost of the form itself. With an argument the pointer is untagged, the matched control (guest_atomic_add_loop.S is the untagged single-instruction loop). Needs top-byte ignore, the emulator's default.

Load-acquire through a top-byte-tagged pointer alone on its page, the cost of the ordered form itself. With an argument the pointer is untagged, the matched control. Needs top-byte ignore, the emulator's default.

SIMD&FP transfers through a top-byte-tagged pointer with the tagged-address ABI enabled, as every Android process with heap pointer tagging makes them. The other vector memory probes use untagged addresses.
Detects regressions in the 4 KiB TLB's index width: two pages half the table's reach apart take separate entries.
Matched control for guest_unscaled_memory_run_loop: the same LDUR- and STUR-family transfers at the same addresses, each through a base register of its own.
Same-base LDUR- and STUR-family transfers at negative offsets from x13, so every transfer after the first of a loop follows one through the same unwritten base.
Matched control for same-page native vector pair transfers.
Matched control for guest_vector_pair_memory_run_loop: the same Q, D and S pair transfers at the same offsets, each through a base register of its own.
Same-base SIMD&FP pairs: four LDP of Q, D, S and Q registers through one base, then four STP through another, so every pair after the first of a loop follows one through the same unwritten base.

Executes five fixed-work samples of 160 million STR S register-offset stores selecting vector_other_store32_x_0, matched instruction-for-instruction with the unsigned-offset probe for cross-host comparison.

Executes five fixed-work samples of 160 million STR S unsigned-offset stores selecting vector_store32_unsigned_fast, matched instruction-for-instruction with the register-offset probe for cross-host comparison.

x86-64 control with no memory access: three blocks joined by two unconditional jumps and the loop branch, each with a never-taken compare-and-branch, all predictable. Runs in an x86-64 guest, as every x86-64 row does.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_call_deep_chain_loop.S: the same 128 functions, calls and returns as eight chains of sixteen.
Calls a chain of 128 x86-64 functions with a frame pointer, each calling the next from its own site, deeper than a return ring or a host return-address stack holds.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_call_leaf_walk_loop.S: the same call sites called in index order, so every call and return is predictable.
Calls eight x86-64 leaves that push and pop a frame from sixty-four sites in a pseudo-random order, so the return's successor is unpredictable, as compiled code calling small functions does.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_call_site_loop.S: the same loop and leaf with the call and the return replaced by direct jumps.
Calls one x86-64 leaf from one site in a loop, so the host predicts the callee and the return's successor. A change to calls and returns must not slow it.

Matched control for guest_x86_64_compare_branch_loop.S: the same compares, moves and never-taken branches with each move between its compare and branch, so the branch reads the compare's flags across the move.

Eight x86-64 register compares against an immediate an iteration, each followed at once by a never-taken conditional branch: the cost of a compare-and-branch pair. guest_x86_64_compare_branch_control_loop.S is its control.

Matched control for guest_x86_64_compare_register_branch_loop.S: the same compares, moves and never-taken branches with each move between its compare and branch, so the branch reads the compare's flags across the move.

Eight x86-64 compares of one register with another an iteration, each followed at once by a never-taken conditional branch: the cost of a register compare-and-branch pair. guest_x86_64_compare_register_branch_control_loop.S is its control.

Eight x86-64 loads and eight stores an iteration, each crossing a page boundary by one to seven bytes, so every access takes the engine's crossing path: what a change to the crossing test costs the accesses that cross.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_flag_overwrite_loop.S: the same producers and moves alternating, so no flag producer is followed at once by another.

Twelve x86-64 register-only arithmetic and logical instructions in a row, each of whose flags the next replaces unread, then twelve flag-neutral moves: the cost of a flag record nothing reads. guest_x86_64_flag_overwrite_control_loop.S is its control.

Matched control for guest_x86_64_link_walk_loop.S: the same blocks and instructions walked in index order, so the linked jumps' successors are predictable and the difference between the two is their misprediction.

Walks sixty-four small x86-64 blocks in a pseudo-random order, two direct jumps a step, each linking to a successor that begins with one of eight families, so both mispredict at a rate the order sets. The branch loop's jumps have one successor each, which the host predicts.
Sixteen 64-bit loads through one base register into four destinations an iteration, each a memory gadget with a fixed successor: the cost of a predicted x86-64 memory gadget and its way out.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_load_walk_loop.S: the same blocks walked in index order, so the load gadget's successor is predictable.

Sixty-four blocks in a pseudo-random order, each entering the same x86-64 load gadget, whose dispatch goes to one of eight register-only families, so it mispredicts at a rate the order sets. The loops' memory gadgets each have one successor, which the host predicts.

x86-64 loads, stores, a load-op, a read-modify-write, a compare against memory with a never-taken branch and a reload of a value just stored, between register arithmetic, as compiled code interleaves them.
x86-64 control with no memory access: sixteen register-only arithmetic, logical, LEA and move instructions an iteration, every final value checked.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_return_conflict_loop.S: the same sites and instructions with return addresses that fold to eight target-table entries, so every return is found there.
Calls one x86-64 leaf from eight sites in a fixed cycle whose return addresses fold to one entry of the address space's target table, so every return finds another site there.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_return_skip_walk_loop.S: the same call sites called in index order.

As guest_x86_64_return_walk_loop.S, but the leaf adds four to its return address, so every return lands one instruction past its call's return address, as a callee that consumes inline arguments does, and a return ring misses it.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_return_walk_loop.S: the same call sites called in index order, so the return's successor is predictable.

Calls one leaf from sixty-four x86-64 sites in a pseudo-random order, so its return, found in the address space's target table, links to one of eight successor families and mispredicts at a rate the order sets.

The sixteen loads of guest_x86_64_load_loop.S with FS and GS overrides, eight each, the bases set by arch_prctl: the ordinary bank's general address path, which adds the segment base, into the translation.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_stack_frame_loop.S: the same instructions, the pushes, pops and RSP arithmetic included, with every other access through another base register.

Opens and closes an x86-64 frame each iteration as compiled code does, two pushes and an RSP subtraction, with spills, reloads into a load-op chain, a 32-bit local, a red-zone store below RSP, a compare against a slot above the frame and a counter in the caller's frame, all through RSP in its own page.
guest_x86_64_load_loop.S with RSP as the base, inside one page and with no push, pop, call or return: the cost of a predicted x86-64 stack load. guest_x86_64_load_loop.S is its control.
guest_x86_64_memory_mix_loop.S with RSP as the base, inside one page and with no push, pop, call or return. guest_x86_64_memory_mix_loop.S is its control.

Sixteen x86-64 loads through RSP an iteration, every one in the page above RSP's, so a path keyed on the stack's page never holds them: what such a path costs the accesses it falls back from. guest_x86_64_stack_span_control_loop.S is its control.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_stack_span_loop.S and guest_x86_64_stack_off_page_loop.S: the same sixteen loads across a page boundary through another base register.
Sixteen x86-64 loads through RSP an iteration from a frame that spans a page boundary, eight in RSP's page and eight in the next.
guest_x86_64_store_loop.S with RSP as the base, inside one page and with no push, pop, call or return: the cost of a predicted x86-64 stack store. guest_x86_64_store_loop.S is its control.
Sixteen 64-bit stores from four registers through one base register an iteration, each a memory gadget that leaves a store on its way to memory, with a fixed successor.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_store_walk_loop.S: the same blocks walked in index order, so the store gadget's successor is predictable.
As guest_x86_64_load_walk_loop.S, but every walk block enters the same x86-64 store gadget, which leaves a store on its way to memory when it dispatches.

Matched control for guest_x86_64_test_self_branch_loop.S: the same TESTs, moves and never-taken branches with each move between its TEST and branch, so the branch reads the TEST's flags across the move.

Eight x86-64 TESTs of a register with itself an iteration, each followed at once by a never-taken conditional branch: the cost of the commonest test-and-branch pair. guest_x86_64_test_self_branch_control_loop.S is its control.
Matched control for guest_x86_64_tlb_direct_alias_loop.S and guest_x86_64_tlb_fold_alias_loop.S: the same sixteen loads from eight neighbouring pages, which any index of the software TLB spreads.
Sixteen x86-64 loads an iteration from eight pages 128 MiB apart, whose page numbers agree in their low fifteen bits: a layout that an index of those bits alone puts in one software-TLB entry.

Sixteen x86-64 loads an iteration from eight pages whose page numbers' low fifteen bits xored with the next fifteen agree: a layout that an index folding those bits so puts in one software-TLB entry and the low bits alone do not.
Contended spin lock whose backoff uses the YIELD hint. The only probe in which a guest thread waits on another, so the only one able to measure guest YIELD lowering.
